stemMd: Which statement must be true in every permitted order?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Birch and Elm must occupy consecutive positions, in either order.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Ash must not be in position 1.

explanationMd:
Combine the ordering and placement constraints rather than assuming one example is unique. The statement "Birch and Elm must occupy consecutive positions, in either order." holds in all 9 permitted orders. Generate the cases by placing any fixed-position item and adjacent block first, then discard arrangements that violate a remaining rule. For each alternative, an explicit permitted counterexample appears in its feedback.

Complete permitted orders (each arrow advances one position):
- Ash → Birch → Elm → Cedar → Fir
- Ash → Birch → Elm → Fir → Cedar
- Ash → Cedar → Birch → Elm → Fir
- Ash → Cedar → Fir → Birch → Elm
- Ash → Fir → Birch → Elm → Cedar
- Ash → Fir → Cedar → Birch → Elm
- Birch → Elm → Ash → Cedar → Fir
- Birch → Elm → Ash → Fir → Cedar
- Birch → Elm → Fir → Ash → Cedar

distractorRationale.c: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Ash → Birch → Elm → Cedar → Fir. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.a: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Ash → Birch → Elm → Cedar → Fir. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.d: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Birch → Elm → Ash → Cedar → Fir. Thus this statement is not necessary.
